method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Prioritization key is defensible, but this is a straightforward new-instability versus unchanged-symptoms item rather than challenge-level integration.
issues: Prioritization key is defensible, but this is a straightforward new-instability versus unchanged-symptoms item rather than challenge-level integration.

items.assessment: Competent worker and established measurement task support assignment while the nurse continues acute respiratory assessment.
Routine discharge instructions are implausible during shock, and the discharge-related objective is unsupported by the current stem.
issues: Routine discharge instructions are implausible during shock, and the discharge-related objective is unsupported by the current stem.
proposedChanges: Replace that distractor with reviewing recent fluid balance; remove awaiting-result from the CBC choice. Add the already planned discharge context if retaining the objective, or align the objective to urgent postoperative deterioration.

items.assessment: Explicit observation frequency, trip duration and qualified escort allow a concrete coordinated solution preserving urgent imaging and surveillance.
Location, emergency response and onset information directly support the immediate telephone emergency; a full history is reasonably deferred.
The stated weekday portal schedule and severe acute symptom support selecting the emergency channel over familiar routine contact routes.
A private acceptable setting addresses nearby listeners; audio-only, shared-device and brief-question shortcuts leave the specific privacy barrier.
Generated-note accuracy is a distinct accountability task; later measurement cannot make an unperformed earlier action true.
Key is correct, but restricted duties is ambiguous: it could mean regulated restricted activities or safely limited nonregulated work.
issues: Key is correct, but restricted duties is ambiguous: it could mean regulated restricted activities or safely limited nonregulated work.
proposedChanges: Replace with an explicit regulated nursing task such as assigning scheduled medication administration while verification is pending.

items.assessment: Consent to treatment and consent to student observation are correctly distinguished; declining observation does not withdraw the accepted care.
A tested effective communication alternative enables participation; caregiver inference and unnecessary repair delay are credible competing arrangements.
Current shock signs and45-minute distance justify supported emergency transport and immediate local care rather than private transport logistics.
Private disclosure of a current destination threat changes transition planning; calling the named person or delaying without resolving location does not address safety.
Adaptive OT plan is good, but all/permanent/every modifiers make alternatives unnecessarily extreme.
issues: Adaptive OT plan is good, but all/permanent/every modifiers make alternatives unnecessarily extreme.
proposedChanges: Use plain plans such as arranging meal delivery, continuing the prior two-handed method, or waiting for dominant-hand recovery; explain the goal mismatch in rationale.

items.assessment: Fasting and meal-linked insulin require a coordinated prescription/glucose/nutrition plan; other safe monitoring and communication steps are appropriately keyed.
Emergency pathway key is appropriate, but all alternatives carry routine/scheduled delay cues.
issues: Emergency pathway key is appropriate, but all alternatives carry routine/scheduled delay cues.
proposedChanges: Use plain competing actions: call usual clinician again, contact covering clinician, repeat observations, or activate the emergency response. Explain why available emergency capability is required by current instability.

items.assessment: Accepted caregiver responsibilities and verified understanding resolve the explicit diffusion-of-responsibility problem better than duplicate instruction or assumed attendance.
Explicit direct-supervision requirement makes consent insufficient by itself; the nursing plan preserves qualified supervision or another competent provider.
The handover principle is useful but assume-routing/file-because-left/family-at-visiting all advertise inadequate follow-up.
issues: The handover principle is useful but assume-routing/file-because-left/family-at-visiting all advertise inadequate follow-up.
proposedChanges: Ask which outcome must be established, with parallel alternatives such as electronic routing, ordering-provider notification, responsible-team receipt, and family notification. The key should be verified receipt by the team currently responsible.

items.assessment: Private preparation, a deliberate pause and confidential follow-up fit the client expressed preference; family presentation conflicts with that request.
The baseline change deserves prompt assessment, but tomorrow/next-scheduled/yesterday-as-current wording creates an easy key.
issues: The baseline change deserves prompt assessment, but tomorrow/next-scheduled/yesterday-as-current wording creates an easy key.
proposedChanges: Present relevant actions directly: repeat vital signs, obtain the family timeline, review previous notes, or assess the new behavioural/neurological change. Preserve first comprehensive bedside assessment as appropriate.

items.assessment: Nonurgent decision timing can be adjusted to permit understanding without presuming incapacity; a signature or later recording does not establish current participation.
Feasible same-day qualified interpreter accommodation preserves privacy and participation; chaperone and family substitution do not necessarily address the preference.
Equivalent in-room therapy with contact precautions meets both rehabilitation and infection-control needs; absence of fever does not negate uncontrolled infectious diarrhea.
Ambiguous false option: immediate authenticated portal release may be appropriate in some systems; the stem does not establish unmet review requirements.
issues: Ambiguous false option: immediate authenticated portal release may be appropriate in some systems; the stem does not establish unmet review requirements.
proposedChanges: State that the current request has not yet completed required identity and third-party information review before asking the SATA, or replace the portal action with an explicitly unauthorized release route.

items.assessment: Time/resource plan is useful, but borrowing a device known unable to provide suction and leaving a request unassigned are cartoon alternatives.
issues: Time/resource plan is useful, but borrowing a device known unable to provide suction and leaving a request unassigned are cartoon alternatives.
proposedChanges: Replace with realistic scheduling/resource proposals, such as moving the routine procedure to another room or requesting the spare unit before allocating the current one; keep immediate airway priority clear.

items.assessment: The freshly assessed modified transfer plan is reasonable, but postponing every practice until full recovery is extreme.
issues: The freshly assessed modified transfer plan is reasonable, but postponing every practice until full recovery is extreme.
proposedChanges: Use a plausible single-session rest or deferral alternative without every/full-recovery qualifiers; keep current assessment and client preference central.

items.assessment: Presenting current assistance needs before final transition decisions appropriately corrects stale functional assumptions.
The explicit15-minute observations and30-minute breaks make accepted coverage necessary; simply timing a break after rounds does not solve the interval gap.
A documented same-agent anaphylaxis warrants clarification despite prior tolerated exposure; communication and the resulting plan are appropriately keyed.
Demonstrated follow-up tasks directly test usability, while grade level, appearance and brevity are credible but indirect proxies.
Time to next feed makes receiving equipment, compatible supplies and competence a concrete handover requirement; sending a manual alone cannot establish readiness.
Navigator availability and interim supplies address both denial resolution and immediate need; the scenario supplies actionable service resources.
Role assignment and confirmation are sound; difficulty challenge overstates the simple explicit duplicate/missing-role problem.
issues: Role assignment and confirmation are sound; difficulty challenge overstates the simple explicit duplicate/missing-role problem.

items.assessment: The key is much longer and only reasonable; calling emergency services because a booking call is late is implausible.
issues: The key is much longer and only reasonable; calling emergency services because a booking call is late is implausible.
proposedChanges: Give a partly complete realistic referral plan and ask which missing safety component should be added, or balance concise competing follow-up plans without every/only and booking-delay emergency-service distractors.

items.assessment: Actual content of care must be verified despite evidence of attendance; assessment of outstanding needs and accurate correction support continuity.
Repeated individual learning need supports private specific feedback and an agreed step; general reminders and policy links are plausible but less targeted.
Acuity-based support is correct, but moving work from the quieter nurse to the already busier nurse is implausible.
issues: Acuity-based support is correct, but moving work from the quieter nurse to the already busier nurse is implausible.
proposedChanges: Replace with a plausible staffing response such as giving the busy nurse unregulated-care support, then explain why current unstable-client surveillance requires qualified support. Remove alone from the proximity option.

items.assessment: Preference-sensitive symptom planning is correct, but before-considering-alternatives/regardless/until-accepts wording makes other options caricatures.
issues: Preference-sensitive symptom planning is correct, but before-considering-alternatives/regardless/until-accepts wording makes other options caricatures.
proposedChanges: Use realistic competing symptom/mobility plans with similar length; distinguish obtaining an acceptable revised plan from repeating persuasion or adapting activity without addressing pain.

items.assessment: Parallel note excerpts discriminate observed/reportable facts from invented causation and timing; the correct uncertainty statement is useful.
This largely repeats156 emergency-channel teaching and uses an every-symptom callback distractor.
issues: This largely repeats156 emergency-channel teaching and uses an every-symptom callback distractor.
proposedChanges: Make the task distinct by verifying reachability of the chosen after-hours plan under a concrete barrier (hearing access, unreliable phone service or caregiver availability), preserving emergency-versus-routine understanding as context.

items.assessment: Goals-based monitoring review is right; stop every assessment because dying is an extreme caricature.
issues: Goals-based monitoring review is right; stop every assessment because dying is an extreme caricature.
proposedChanges: Replace with a plausible independent switch to symptom-triggered overnight observations and explain why the active order should be reviewed with the team rather than changed unilaterally.

items.assessment: An available entrance directly matches the requested trauma-related accommodation; grounding, reminder and accompaniment are plausible competing supports.
Current delivery, findings and trend directly establish receiving respiratory needs; historical diagnosis/imaging/home logistics are credible lower-priority information.
Explicit participation mismatch makes applicability the first appraisal issue; effect size, sample size and training are meaningful competing evidence concerns.
New repeated swallowing symptoms and a stalled referral warrant current safety assessment and an interim plan rather than repeated routine referral or independent texture prescription.
Demonstrated wound independence does not resolve ongoing entry/exit needs; a one-time assisted arrival is a plausible but incomplete discharge solution.
The scheduling solution is sound, but the retained objective/takeaway discusses a declined service and closed referral absent from the rewritten case.
issues: The scheduling solution is sound, but the retained objective/takeaway discusses a declined service and closed referral absent from the rewritten case.
proposedChanges: Change objective and takeaway to coordinating a flexible home-care visit around fixed dialysis transport while preserving the client preferred setting.

items.assessment: Applying symptom scenarios directly measures the missing decision skill rather than number recall, confidence or receipt documentation.
Shared-process review is appropriate, but only in the staff-presence alternative advertises insufficiency.
issues: Shared-process review is appropriate, but only in the staff-presence alternative advertises insufficiency.
proposedChanges: Use the plain alternative reviewing staff-assignment records for each omission; explain why mapping the shared coverage process better addresses the recurring unassigned-role pattern.
